topic: The Dark History of Vice City (3D-universe deep dive, GTA VI framing)
scope: Deep dive on the 3D-universe (1980s) Vice City from Vice City Stories (1984) and Vice City (1986), framed for GTA VI audiences: the HD-universe Vice City appears only in the opening and closing, at setting level (spoiler 'none'). The 2D original is mentioned only as real-world history.

claims.text: Grand Theft Auto VI launched on November 19, 2026.
Take-Two reported about $3.79 billion in GTA VI sales by the end of launch day, a company estimate.
Vice City first appeared in the original Grand Theft Auto in 1997, in the separate top-down (2D) continuity.
The 1980s Vice City of the 3D games is a fictional city modeled on Miami.
GTA VI is set in the fictional state of Leonida, with Vice City as its central city.
Rockstar's own description calls GTA VI's Vice City 'the darkest side of the sunniest place in America'.
GTA VI's protagonists are Jason and Lucia.
Vice City Stories is set in 1984, two years before Vice City.
The game's own framing presents 1984 Vice City as a boomtown whose growth is fueled by the drug trade, a city built on crime and betrayal.
Victor 'Vic' Vance is a U.S. Army corporal stationed at Fort Baxter in Vice City.
Vic's sergeant, Jerry Martinez, runs a secret drug business, then frames Vic for drugs and for bringing a prostitute onto the base, and Vic is dishonorably discharged.
The cocaine Vic and Lance steal from Martinez turns out to belong to the Mendez brothers, Armando and Diego; Martinez was only moving it for them.
In 1984 the Mendez brothers are the city's most powerful drug kingpins, while presenting themselves publicly as philanthropists.
Ricardo Diaz, a rival drug baron, employs the Vance brothers against the Mendez operation.
After using the Vance brothers for a few jobs, the Mendez brothers betray them, and the Vances go to war with the cartel.
The war costs Vic dearly: Louise dies after the Mendez brothers kidnap her, Armando is killed at the Mendez mansion, and Vic kills Diego and Martinez on the roof of the Mendez Building.
Between 1984 and 1986 Diaz establishes himself as Vice City's dominant drug baron.
Tommy Vercetti served fifteen years in prison for the killings in Harwood, Liberty City, and the press called him 'the Harwood Butcher'.
In 1986 Sonny Forelli sends the newly released Tommy to Vice City to oversee a drug deal and expand the family's business south.
The deal is ambushed: Victor Vance and two Forelli men, Harry and Lee, are killed, the money and cocaine are taken, and Tommy, Ken Rosenberg and Lance escape.
While working for Diaz, Tommy and Lance learn that Diaz's people were behind the ambush.
Tommy and Lance storm Diaz's mansion on Starfish Island and kill him, and Tommy takes the mansion and Diaz's empire.
Sonny Forelli comes to Vice City to collect money he considers his; Lance reveals Tommy's plan to Sonny, and Tommy kills both of them in the final mission.
In the finale Tommy accuses Sonny of sending him to Harwood after a man who knew he was coming; Sonny deflects rather than denies, and claims Tommy's fifteen years in prison were his to spend.
claims.notes: Checked against a fan transcript (S29): the dialogue implies, but does not state, that Sonny set Tommy up. Confirm in the cutscene.

claims.text: Lance's betrayal grew out of feeling underappreciated and sidelined in Tommy's rise; in the game he only calls it business.
Some players believe Sonny Forelli, not Diaz, arranged the ambush to get rid of Tommy.
After Sonny's death, Marco Forelli becomes the family's new don.
By 1992 Ken has been through rehab, lost his law license and is running Caligula's Palace casino in Las Venturas for three mafia families.
Ken's cocaine addiction drives a rift with Tommy; after Ken's rehab, Tommy stops taking his calls.
claims.notes: Per the wiki, the Tommy detail comes from San Andreas' 'The Introduction'. Confirm there.

claims.text: Whether anything from 1980s Vice City carries over into GTA VI's Vice City is unconfirmed; the two may share only a name.
Vic joined the army to pay for his brother Pete's asthma medication.
Vic ends 1984 wealthy and wanting out of the drug trade, but Lance pulls him back in, leading to the 1986 deal with the Forellis.
Retired colonel Juan Garcia Cortez helped set up the 1986 exchange, and afterwards promises Tommy he will find out who was behind the ambush.
Cortez has Tommy kill Gonzalez, a former associate blamed for the deal going wrong; wiki accounts say Gonzalez had leaked the deal to Diaz.
claims.notes: The leak detail rests on one wiki (S34); narrate it as 'reportedly' unless confirmed in-game.

claims.text: Real-estate developer Avery Carrington has Tommy, disguised as a Cuban gang member, kill the new Haitian ganglord at a funeral, starting a gang war to drive down property prices.
Vice City's 1986 property boom was built in part on deliberately started gang violence.
Wiki accounts treat Sonny's earlier Harwood setup as fact; the game itself only implies it.
